lines.english: ............The bathroom...

lines.japanese: ……あー、便所……。
lines.english: ...Right. The bathroom...

lines.japanese: ……アレキサンダーの便所か。
lines.english: ...Alexander's bathroom, huh.

lines.japanese: ……ふう。
lines.english: ...Phew.

lines.japanese: いつもの服に着替えて洗面所を出た俺は、まず第一に店内の壁時計を見上げた。
lines.english: Back in my usual clothes, I came out of the washroom and looked straight at the clock on the wall.

lines.japanese: 午後８時ちょい過ぎ。約束の時間よりすこし早かった（よし、やつにしちゃ上出来だ）。
lines.english: A little after eight in the evening. A little earlier than we’d agreed. (Good. For him, downright impressive.)

lines.japanese: 次に、フロアを見渡して使いなれたあのスポーツバッグを探した。
lines.english: Next, I scanned the floor for that familiar sports bag.

lines.japanese: ──あった。カウンター席の足元。俺は濡れた手からぷらぷら水を切りつつ近付いていった。
lines.english: —There it was, beneath a counter seat. I walked over, flicking the water from my hands.

lines.japanese: カウンターテーブルには空っぽのコーヒーカップとクリアファイル、それから小さなクリップボードに挟まれた伝票が置かれていた。
lines.english: On the counter sat an empty coffee cup, a clear plastic folder, and a check clipped to a little board.

lines.japanese: ……伝票？
lines.english: ...A check?

lines.japanese: クリアファイルはバッグに押しこみ、伝票の方は──破りすてたいけど我慢した。
lines.english: I stuffed the clear folder into my bag. The check, though—I wanted to rip it up, but held myself back.

lines.japanese: 「んー？　帰んの？」
lines.english: “Hmm? Leaving?”

lines.japanese: その紙きれをいまいましげに睨んでいると、店員が店員とは思えない無作法な声をかけてきた。
lines.english: As I glared at the hated scrap of paper, the waitress called over in a tone no self-respecting waitress would use.

lines.japanese: 俺は頷く代わりに、無言で伝票を突きだした。女はちょっと面くらった顔をしたけど、もぐように受けると、レジへ向かって歩いていった。俺もあとに続いた。
lines.english: Instead of nodding, I silently thrust the check at her. She looked briefly taken aback, then plucked it from my hand and walked to the register. I followed.
“Three twenty.”

lines.japanese: レジでバーコードを読んだあと、女が表示された緑色の数字をぶっきらぼうに告げた。俺は財布から出した小銭を受け皿に叩きつけた。釣りはいらねえぜ。
lines.english: After scanning the barcode, she bluntly read off the green number on the display. I slammed a handful of coins from my wallet into the tray. Keep the change.

lines.japanese: 「はい、丁度どうもー」
lines.english: “Exact change. Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 女はボタンひとつでレシートを打ちだし、ぴっと横へ引いて差しだした。俺もぴっと横から受けとって背を向けた。
lines.english: She printed the receipt at the touch of a button, tore it off with a sharp sideways flick, and held it out. I took it with an equally sharp flick and turned away.

lines.japanese: 「毎度ー。また明日なー」
lines.english: “Thanks. See you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 店を出るとき、ちょっとだけ温度の高い声が投げかけられた。どうでもいい。俺は返事をしなかった。
lines.english: As I left, she tossed after me a voice half a degree warmer than before. I didn't care. I gave no answer.

lines.japanese: 「さて」
lines.english: “Now, then.”

lines.japanese: いつもの現場に入るまで、あと３時間近くもある。思いがけないボーナスタイムだ。どうっすかな。適当にぶらぶら歩くか。
lines.english: I’ve still got almost three hours before I have to be at my usual job site. Unexpected bonus time. So what now? Guess I’ll just wander around.

lines.japanese: 夜の柳木原は、あてがないときの散歩道としちゃそれなりに面白いスポットだ。見所は多いし、眺めは日々移ろうし、ときにはヒューマンドラマに遭遇したりもする。金なんかなくても退屈はしない。
lines.english: Yanagihara after dark made a decent walk when you had nowhere to go. There was plenty to see, the scenery changed by the day, and sometimes you stumbled into a whole human drama. You could keep yourself entertained without spending a yen.

lines.japanese: まあ、あればそりゃ、もっと楽しくはなるだろうけどさ。
lines.english: Though obviously, money would make it more fun.

lines.japanese: 「そんでここか」
lines.english: “And this is where I end up.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだい、来るなり感じの悪い坊主だね」
lines.english: “What a charming thing to say the moment you get here, kid.”

lines.japanese: 見所の多いこの街で探しあてたのは、しかし見飽きたピンク色のバンだった。
lines.english: Yet in a city with so much to see, what I’d managed to find was that same old pink van.

lines.japanese: もちろんクレープを食いに来たわけじゃない。小銭稼ぎの仕事を求めて来ただけだ。
lines.english: Naturally, I hadn't come for a crêpe. I was only looking for some little job to earn pocket money.

lines.japanese: つーても、ここんとこ便利屋の仕事やってねえなあ。依頼の件数自体が減ってきてるし、その中でなお残ってる業務内容となれば、ぶっちゃけろくなもんがない。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I hadn’t had much handyman work lately. The requests themselves were drying up, and frankly, what little remained wasn’t worth a damn.

lines.japanese: 「パルさん、成田工務店に仕事入ってねえの。もうなんでもやるぜ、健全な仕事なら」
lines.english: “Paru, doesn’t Narita Construction have any work? I’ll do anything at this point—as long as it’s honest work.”

lines.japanese: 「あるよ、ド健全なのが」
lines.english: “I do. One so wholesome it hurts.”

lines.japanese: あるのか。じゃ、いまの間はなんだ。
lines.english: She did? Then what was that pause for?

lines.japanese: 「でも、どうしたもんかねえ」
lines.english: “But I don't know if I should give it to you.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なにそれ。なんか裏でもあんの」
lines.english: “What? Is there some kind of catch?”

lines.japanese: 俺は身を乗りだして尋ねたが、しかし正直なところ期待はしていなかった。だって本当にいい仕事があるなら、パルさんだってこんな風に勿体つけたりはしないだろう。
lines.english: I leaned forward to ask, though honestly I wasn't getting my hopes up. If the job were truly good, Paru wouldn't be dangling it in front of me like this.

lines.japanese: 「作業内容は。依頼主は。金の払いは」
lines.english: “What's the work? Who's hiring? What does it pay?”

lines.japanese: 「手作業・座り仕事。大手優良企業。一晩で一万ちょい」
lines.english: “Work with your hands. Seated. Major, reputable company. A little over ten thousand yen for the night.”

lines.japanese: 「まじで」
lines.english: “Seriously?”

lines.japanese: すげえいい条件。つまり、逆に言えばうさんくせえ。
lines.english: The terms were so good they made the whole thing shady as hell.

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ大手って。どこそれ」
lines.english: “What major company? Which one?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、あっこに看板かかってんだろ。あのビルのてっぺんから、ひい、ふう、三番目」
lines.english: “See the signs over there? Count down from the top of that building. One, two... third.”

lines.japanese: 「三番目……へっ」
lines.english: “Third... Huh.”

lines.japanese: そこには、このところ新聞や電車の中吊り広告なんかでよく見る、ＩＴだか何だかっぽい企業の社名が燦然と輝いていた。
lines.english: There, shining in all its glory, was the name of some vaguely techy corporation I'd been seeing everywhere lately, in newspapers and ads on the train.

lines.japanese: 「あ、知ってる、あの会社。え、クライアントあそこなの。マジで」
lines.english: “Oh, I know that company. They're the client? Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「あたしが嘘言ってどうすんだい」
lines.english: “Why would I lie to you?”

lines.japanese: 「お、ちょー待てよ。なら文句ねーって、早くその仕事くれよ。なんで躊躇してんだよ」
lines.english: “Whoa, wait. Then I've got no complaints. Give me the job already. Why are you hesitating?”

lines.japanese: 「ってやんでい、あんたが来るなり感じ悪いからだろ」
lines.english: “Don’t give me that—you’re the one who showed up with a rotten attitude.”

lines.japanese: 「おい美人パティシエ。ください。仕事を紹介してください」
lines.english: “Beautiful pastry chef. Please. Kindly get me that job.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふん、結構じゃないか。やりゃあできんだ、ええッ？　いいかい、おまえさんがいッつもそんな態度なら、こっちだって気持ーちよく仕事の紹介がしてやれんのさ。いいねッ？」
lines.english: “Hmph. Much better. See? You can do it when you try. If you always behaved this way, I could enjoy finding work for you too. Understand?”

lines.japanese: こんなんでいいのか。俺は仲介人に対する態度をほんの少しだけ改めてもいいかなと思った。
lines.english: That was all it took? I considered improving my attitude toward my broker by the smallest imaginable degree.

lines.japanese: 「つーわけで、おい美人パティシエ。ください。はやく仕事を紹介してください」
lines.english: “So, beautiful pastry chef. Please. Hurry up and get me that job.”

lines.japanese: 「んじゃドラ、あんたスーツとか持ってるかい？」
lines.english: “All right, Dora. Do you own a suit?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　なんで。これなら持ってるけど」
lines.english: “Huh? Why? I've got this right here.”

lines.japanese: 俺はスポーツバッグの口を開け、野良犬色の作業着を引っぱりあげて見せた。
lines.english: I opened my sports bag and held up my stray-dog-colored work clothes.

lines.japanese: 「……なんだい、それ」
lines.english: “...What is that?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、鼻押さえなくていいから。見りゃ分かんだろ、俺の仕事着だよ」
lines.english: “You don't have to hold your nose. One look tells you what they are: my work clothes.”

lines.japanese: 「あのね、あんたね、あたしゃいまスーツって言ったんだよ。背広、ジャケット、ビジネスマンの仕事着」
lines.english: “Listen. I said a suit. Business suit. Jacket. A businessman's work clothes.”

lines.japanese: 「ばかおまえ、これこそ男の仕事着だっつうの。てめブルーカラーなめんな。あとおまえ、鼻は押さえなくていいから」
lines.english: “Idiot, these are a real man's work clothes. Don't disrespect blue-collar labor. And stop holding your nose.”

lines.japanese: 「いやね、実は昔の同級生に一人さ、あっこに就職しちまいやがった小偉い男がいンのよ。野郎と来たら、これが一丁前に、あの頃ちょいとあたしにホの字だよ、なッ？　ところがだ、こっからが大変だよお立会い」
lines.english: “See, an old classmate of mine got himself a job over there and rose high enough to become a minor big shot. And wouldn’t you know, the bastard had a bit of a crush on me back then. But gather round, folks, because here’s where it gets serious.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょーちょー、待てよ。何ありもしない過去バナ勝手に始めてんだよ。いいから仕事の話進めろよ。あとおまえ、鼻は押さえなくていいから」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa, whoa. Why are you launching into some made-up story about a past that never happened? Get on with the job. And stop holding your nose.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、仕事？　ああ、そうか……」
lines.english: “Oh, the job? Right...”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だからあっこは、そんな急に図体ばっかりスクすくスクすく育っちまった会社なもんで、まァ人手が足りない足りない他力本願とくらあ。そんでホラ、そこのビルの──」
lines.english: “Well, that company shot up so fast—grew and grew until it was all body and no brains—that now they're always short-handed. No, sir. Can't do a thing without outside help. So, in that building over there—”

lines.japanese: パルさんの指の先を見上げる。天空に刺さるアルバトロス。
lines.english: I followed Paru's pointing finger upward. Albatross speared the heavens.

lines.japanese: 「──あっこン中に入ってる、なんだ、ビーだかブーだか言ったか、そんなドでかいショップのシステム入力に猫の手もお貸しいただきたいと、野郎がこう言ってるわけよ。でドラ、あんたパソコンって使えたっけ？」
lines.english: “—there's some enormous shop in there called B-something or Boo-something. The bastard says they're desperate enough to borrow a cat's paw just to enter data into its system. So, Dora, can you use a computer?”

lines.japanese: 「おい美人パティシエ。ください。他の仕事を紹介してください」
lines.english: “Beautiful pastry chef. Please. Kindly find me another job.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、やっぱ触った事もないか」
lines.english: “Ah. Never touched one, huh? Thought so.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、待てよ。やっぱッてなんだよ、なんで分かんだよ。読むな。俺の心を読むな」
lines.english: “Wait. What's *thought so* supposed to mean? How'd you know? Quit reading my mind.”

lines.japanese: 「はン、まあ、いいさね。あたしも大して期待してたわけじゃないよ」
lines.english: “Hmph. Fine. It's not as though I expected much.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、ちょっとは期待してたわけ。しょーがねえな、じゃあいっちょ気合入れて頑張ってやるよ。どうなの、パソコンとかって、わりと難しいわけ」
lines.english: “What, so you did expect something? Fine. I'll buckle down and do it. How hard can computer stuff be, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、もしあんたが一晩のうちチンパンジー程度の入力でも出来るようンなったら、明日の夜８時きっかりにあたしンとこ来な」
lines.english: “If you can learn to enter data even at chimpanzee level in one night, come here tomorrow at eight sharp.”
“Eight tomorrow night—”

lines.japanese: 考える余地もなかった。その時刻、俺は柳木原にいない。がっかりしたようなほっとしたような、なんとも言いがたい感覚に襲われた。
lines.english: There was nothing to consider. At that hour, I wouldn't be in Yanagihara. I was struck by an indescribable sensation, equal parts disappointment and relief.

lines.japanese: 「──ああ悪い、せっかくだけど、そら時間的に無理だわ。ＩＴ的には一晩でおおむねなんとか出来ンだけど、まあ時間的な都合がな。あァ、いくら俺がＩＴの天才でも、神の領域は無理だわ」
lines.english: “—Sorry. Great offer, but the timing makes it impossible. IT-wise, I could more or less handle it overnight, but schedule-wise, you know. Even an IT genius like me can't rewrite time. That's God's department.”

lines.japanese: 「はいはい、っと」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah. Moving on.”

lines.japanese: 「さあドラ、用が済んだならァ、とっとと帰ってくんな。こちとら、こっからが稼ぎ時だよ」
lines.english: “Now, Dora, if you're finished here, hurry up and clear out. This is when the money starts coming in.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、おう」
lines.english: “Yeah, sure.”

lines.japanese: 振りかえれば品の良さそうな学生カップルが、俺の体という障害物を煩わしげに避けて、移動式クレープ店のメニュー表を覗きこんでいた。
lines.english: When I turned, a refined-looking student couple was peering at the mobile crêpe stand’s menu, edging irritably around the obstacle my body presented.

lines.japanese: 俺はバンに背中を向けると、カップルの視界から外れてそれとなく街の風景の一部に戻った。
lines.english: I turned my back on the van, slipped from the couple's field of vision, and unobtrusively resumed my place as part of the city scenery.

lines.japanese: それから本屋の怪談コーナーでＩＴ系の書籍を立ち読みし、充分に時間を潰してから現場へ入った。
lines.english: Afterward, I stood reading an IT book in the bookstore’s ghost-story section. Once I’d killed enough time, I reported to the job site.

lines.japanese: タイトルは『インターネットの世界であった本当に怖い話』だけど文句あるか？
lines.english: The title was *True Tales of Terror from the World of the Internet*. Got a problem with that?
